stemMd: A company says its training programme is effective because participants’ average sales rose afterward. Which question is most useful for evaluating the claim?

options.label: A
options.textMd: How many pages were in the company’s annual report?

options.label: C
options.textMd: What colour was the training room?

options.label: D
options.textMd: Did sales rise similarly among comparable employees who did not take the programme?

options.label: E
options.textMd: Did the programme title contain the word success?

explanationMd: Sales could rise because of market demand, seasonality or company-wide changes. Comparing similar nonparticipants helps estimate what might have happened without training. The relevant evidence concerns outcomes under a plausible comparison, not presentation details.

distractorRationale.c: Room colour is not directly relevant to the causal claim.
distractorRationale.a: Report length does not isolate the training effect.
distractorRationale.e: A title is not evidence of effectiveness.
distractorRationale.b: Name ordering does not explain sales changes.
